channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan begin in Russian capital
item.description: The eighth Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan commenced in Moscow, gathering regional countries and Afghanistan to discuss security and economic cooperation. Representatives from Afghanistan, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan are attending. Belarus and Egypt are guests.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens International Cooperation in Education Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing international educational cooperation, focusing on participation in global achievement assessments and adopting best practices. The country is attending the 67th General Assembly of the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA) in Warsaw. Discussions include IEA's strategic directions, PIRLS and TIMSS research, and new initiatives. Uzbekistan's National Institute of Pedagogical Skills named after A. Avloni is seeking IEA membership.

item.title: Regional Economic Ties Expand with New Directions and Markets
item.description: Economic ties in the region are growing, with increased trade, new transport routes, and investment projects. Cooperation within the Eurasian space, including the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), is developing. The SCO's 'SCO-2040' initiative focuses on industrial cooperation, transport connectivity, and financing mechanisms. Uzbekistan's trade with EAEU countries significantly increased between 2017 and 2025.

item.title: Major projects in the oil and gas sector reviewed
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed a presentation on major projects in Uzbekistan's oil and gas sector. The review covered the implementation of recent decrees aimed at improving Uzbekneftegaz's operations and procurement. Plans for increasing gas reserves through expanded geological exploration and drilling were also discussed.

item.title: Taliban: International Criminal Court not recognized
item.description: The Taliban spokesperson stated Afghanistan does not recognize the International Criminal Court (ICC) or its rulings. This follows the ICC's announcement of arrest warrants for the Taliban's leader and three other officials. The ICC alleges they are criminally responsible for persecution based on gender against women and girls.

item.title: Turkey and Pakistan to send troops to Saudi Arabia under Mecca defense pact
item.description: In response to escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan will deploy forces under the Mecca defense pact. This decision was made at an emergency meeting in Riyadh. The pact aims to enhance military readiness and collective capabilities to counter threats and ensure regional security.

item.title: Driver Hits Two Children and Flees Scene in Almaty Region, Later Apprehended
item.description: A driver in the Almaty region struck two children sitting by the roadside and fled the scene. Police later apprehended a 65-year-old suspect. One of the injured children remains in serious condition following surgery. A criminal case has been initiated regarding the hit-and-run incident.

item.title: Police Officer Fatally Attacked After Issuing Warning in Oskemen
item.description: A police officer in Oskemen died after being assaulted following an intervention. The incident occurred at an entertainment venue where the off-duty officer warned an unruly individual. The suspect, who also injured another patron, has been arrested. The police department confirmed the deceased was an officer.

item.title: Police officer dies after confronting cafe patron in Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: A 40-year-old police officer died in Ust-Kamenogorsk after confronting a patron in a cafe. The officer, off-duty, reportedly made a remark to a patron behaving inappropriately. The patron allegedly pursued him outside and kicked him in the face, causing fatal injuries. A suspect has been detained.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry Responds to Latvia's Visa Restriction Proposal
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has commented on Latvia's proposal to restrict visas for Uzbek citizens. A ministry representative stated that Uzbekistan began taking diplomatic measures as soon as news of the visa restriction plans emerged. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: ICC Issues Arrest Warrants for Taliban Education Ministers
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has issued arrest warrants for Habibullah Agha and Neda Mohammad Nadeem, the Taliban's Ministers of Education and Higher Education, respectively. The warrants, unsealed on October 5, 2025, are for crimes against humanity, specifically persecution targeting women and girls.

item.title: Yemen's War: A Complex Intersection of Poverty, Internal Divisions, and Regional Rivalry
item.description: Yemen's current crisis is a result of economic poverty, deep internal divisions, and regional rivalries. The conflict stems from severe poverty, political deadlock, the rise of the Houthis, and the country becoming a stage for proxy wars among regional powers, despite its historical significance.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Meets Russian Counterpart to Discuss Bilateral Ties and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's foreign minister, held discussions with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov regarding bilateral relations and the expansion of economic and trade cooperation. The Taliban's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that regional issues and ongoing political consultations were also addressed. Muttaqi emphasized strengthening political understanding and increasing cooperation in economic, trade, and transit sectors.

item.title: New Appointments Made in Uzbekistan's Higher Education and Preschool Education Ministries
item.description: Qongirotboy Sharipov and E'zozxon Karimova have been appointed to new positions. Previously, Sharipov served as the Minister of Higher Education, Science, and Innovations, while Karimova was the Minister of Preschool and School Education. These appointments signal potential shifts in the leadership of Uzbekistan's educational sectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Appoints New Vice-Ministers and Dismisses Others
item.description: Kazakhstan's government has announced several personnel changes. A new Vice-Minister of Justice has been appointed, and a new head of the Apparatus has taken office at the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Several Vice-Ministers have also been dismissed from their posts, according to Egemen.kz.

item.title: Uzbekistan MFA Responds to Latvian Interior Ministry's Visa Proposal
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry has responded to Latvia's Interior Ministry's proposal to temporarily restrict visas for Uzbek citizens. Latvia suggested the restriction due to alleged crimes committed by some Uzbek citizens after arrival. The proposal was not discussed at a government meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Discuss Agricultural Cooperation and Solar Energy in Fergana Valley
item.description: Uzbekistan's Fergana region is implementing innovative viticulture technologies, utilizing solar energy to offset gardening costs. A company, AOK GARDEN LLC, showcased its 110-hectare project featuring 10,000 solar panels generating 5 MW. Participants of the Uzbekistan-Russia Regional Council meeting visited the facility, learning about grape cultivation, drip irrigation, and processing.

item.title: Three Iranian Citizens Sentenced for Illegal Fishing and Border Crossing in Kazakhstan
item.description: Three Iranian nationals were apprehended by Kazakh border guards for illegally crossing the state border while fishing in the Caspian Sea. A criminal case was initiated for illegal border crossing by a group. The Karakiya District Court found the Iranians guilty, sentencing each to one year in prison, followed by deportation. The sentences are not yet legally binding.

item.title: Afghanistan Faces Potential Shortage of Female Teachers Due to Education Restrictions
item.description: Education activists warn that barring girls from education in Afghanistan could lead to a severe shortage of female teachers in the coming years. Universities and training centers remain closed to women, preventing new personnel from entering the profession. Current female teachers may also leave their posts, exacerbating the problem and potentially jeopardizing girls' access to education, especially in rural areas.

item.title: India Exports Akash Missile System to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan
item.description: India has exported its Akash surface-to-air missile system to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, according to Indian Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. The system is designed to counter threats like drones and aircraft. This marks an expansion of Indian arms exports into markets traditionally supplied by Russia.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations Announces New Appointment
item.description: Major General Margulan Amanbayev has been appointed head of the apparatus for Kazakhstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES). Previously, he led the emergency situations department for the Karaganda region. Amanbayev, 53, has a long career in civil protection, holding various leadership roles since 2000.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Reviews Educational Reforms at New Uzbekistan University
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the New Uzbekistan University to review educational reforms and future plans. Exhibits showcased transformations from early childhood development to professional training, emphasizing education as a unified system. The President also discussed digital transformation and new assessment methods for schools.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Enhance Cooperation in Mining Industry
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey are strengthening cooperation in the mining and geology sectors. The Minister of Mining and Geology of Uzbekistan met with a delegation from Turkey's Nakkaş Holding to discuss joint investment projects, expanding the mineral resource base, and creating new production capacities.

item.title: Turkistan Region to Provide 24-Hour Drinking Water to 10 Settlements by 2026
item.description: In the Turkistan region, 801 settlements are already supplied with drinking water. A plan for 2026-2028 aims to resolve issues with water supply to 155 settlements where water is currently provided on a schedule. By 2026, 10 settlements with 45,700 residents will receive uninterrupted 24-hour water supply. Funding is allocated for infrastructure upgrades.

item.title: Russian and Taliban Foreign Ministers Meet on Sidelines of Moscow Format Talks
item.description: The Foreign Ministers of Russia and the Taliban held a meeting on the sidelines of the 'Moscow Format' consultations. The specifics of the discussions were not immediately disclosed, but the meeting signifies diplomatic engagement between the two parties.

item.title: UN Envoy Urges Progress on Women's Rights During Afghanistan Visit
item.description: A United Nations envoy has urged progress on women's rights during a visit to Afghanistan. The envoy also reaffirmed the UN's readiness to support Afghans returning from neighboring countries. The visit aimed to encourage improvements in the human rights situation for women.

item.title: Teachers Demoralized by Pay Cuts and Economic Pressure on World Teachers' Day
item.description: On World Teachers' Day, teachers in Kabul public schools report demoralization due to low salaries, pay cuts, and rising living costs. Many face economic and psychological pressure, forcing some to quit or seek second jobs. Issues like heavy workloads, delayed payments, and large class sizes exacerbate difficulties.

item.title: India and Afghanistan Maintain Contact Through UN Channels Amidst Regional Tensions
item.description: India's Deputy Foreign Minister met with the UN Special Representative for Afghanistan, signaling India's approach of supporting the Afghan people via international channels without direct involvement in political or security disputes. The meeting stressed humanitarian needs and UNAMA's role, highlighting India's continued engagement amidst Afghanistan's severe humanitarian and economic challenges.

item.title: UN Human Rights Council Extends Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett's Afghanistan Mandate for One Year
item.description: The UN Human Rights Council has extended the mandate of Richard Bennett, the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, for an additional year. Bennett confirmed the decision, noting the extension includes an enhanced dialogue in June 2027 focusing on gender-related concerns and a study on minorities.

item.title: Afghanistan and Russia Discuss Expanding Bilateral Ties and Regional Stability
item.description: Afghanistan's Foreign Minister met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow to discuss bilateral relations, economic cooperation, and regional developments. Both sides expressed interest in deepening political understanding and expanding trade ties. Russia acknowledged Afghanistan's efforts in counter-narcotics and security issues, with discussions also covering regional stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Increase Refinery Capacity to 65% by Year-End
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to boost the utilization rate of the Fergana Oil Refinery (FNQIZ) from 40% to 65% by the end of the year, with further increases planned later. This was announced during a presentation on oil and gas industry projects to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The refinery's main technological units have been repaired, increasing diesel production by 30%, bitumen by 60%, and aviation fuel fivefold.

item.title: Police Officer Fatally Injured After Making Remark in Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: A police officer died in Ust-Kamenogorsk after being assaulted for making a remark to a patron in an establishment. The incident occurred on the night of October 4th. The suspect, who was off-duty at the time, has been detained. Another patron was also injured. Authorities are investigating the criminal case.

item.title: Driver Hits Children on Roadside in Almaty Region and Flees Scene
item.description: A driver in the Almaty region struck two children sitting on the roadside with a Cobalt vehicle and fled the scene. A video of the incident circulated on social media. The 65-year-old driver has been identified and apprehended. Pre-trial investigation has begun, and the children are undergoing surgery.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Highlight Common Themes at UN General Assembly
item.description: All five Central Asian nations participated in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. Their representatives addressed regional cooperation, security, conflicts, UN and Security Council reform, and environmental issues. They also proposed establishing new structures under UN auspices. Uzbekistan was represented by Saida Mirziyoyeva, Kyrgyzstan by President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Global grain prices could surge 80% due to Strait of Hormuz disruptions, experts warn
item.description: Disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz could trigger a global food crisis, with experts predicting grain prices may increase by up to 80% in some regions. Approximately one-third of fertilizer shipments also pass through this route, and logistical bottlenecks have already reduced export volumes by 40%. The El Niño phenomenon is exacerbating the situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Experience in Constitutional Justice Development in the Digital Age
item.description: Kazakhstan shared its experience in developing constitutional justice during the digital era at the VII Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts and Equivalent Institutions in Samarkand. The Congress adopted the Samarkand Declaration, focusing on human rights protection and the rule of law in the digital environment.

item.title: Abror Po'latov Appointed Deputy Head of Presidential Administration's Secretariat
item.description: Abror Po'latov has been appointed Deputy Head of the Secretariat of the Head of the Presidential Administration. He graduated from Tashkent Islamic University in 2006 and Uzbekistan National University (Master's) in 2008. He holds a Doctor of Philosophy in Political Sciences.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Ties with Asia, Promotes Cultural and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding cooperation with international partners in investment, technology, business, and culture. The country participated in the ASEAN Film Festival in Hong Kong and opened an Honorary Consulate in Daejeon, South Korea. Discussions were held with Hong Kong manufacturers regarding potential investments in Kazakhstan's machine-building, light, and chemical industries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discovers Five New Gas Fields Since Start of Year
item.description: Uzbekistan has discovered five new natural gas fields since the beginning of the year, according to a presentation to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Eighty wells have been drilled, with plans for 40 more in the fourth quarter. Geological exploration is expanding to boost gas reserves.

item.title: Driver Without License Arrested Again in Akmola Region for Drunk Driving
item.description: Police in Esil, Akmola Region, detained a 49-year-old man driving under the influence of alcohol, despite having his license previously revoked. The man was found to be in a moderate state of intoxication. He had previously been caught for a similar offense in January 2025 and was sentenced to seven years without driving privileges.
